Our culture 
At 1Password, we prioritize collaboration, clear and transparent communication, receptiveness to feedback, and alignment with our core values: keep it simple, lead with honesty, and put people first.

Position Summary 
 As Product Owner for Sadie, you will be responsible for turning our product vision and roadmap into clearly defined, deliverable product outcomes.
 You will work closely with management, customers, engineering, design, and commercial teams to understand what needs to be built, define how it should work, and ensure it is delivered successfully.
 A major part of your role will be translating product ideas and customer problems into clear requirements, workflows, tickets, acceptance criteria, and expected behaviours that engineering can execute against.
 You will own the detail behind the roadmap and ensure what we ship fulfils the original product and customer intent.
 Values 
 Excellent communication and collaboration skills
 Strong ownership and accountability
 Customer-focused and outcome-driven
 Highly organized with strong attention to detail
 Comfortable challenging assumptions and asking questions
 Open to feedback and continuous improvement
 High degree of integrity, professionalism, and discretion
 What You’ll Be Doing 
 Work closely with management to translate the Sadie product vision and roadmap into actionable product initiatives.
 Own and maintain the product backlog, ensuring priorities are clearly defined and aligned with the roadmap.
 Break larger product initiatives into clear requirements, user stories, workflows, tickets, and acceptance criteria.
 Define exactly how Sadie should behave across different customer scenarios and edge cases.
 Ensure engineering has the context and requirements needed to build features correctly without ambiguity.
 Work closely with engineering throughout development to answer questions, resolve ambiguity, make trade-offs, and keep delivery aligned with the intended product outcome.
 Review and validate completed work against requirements and acceptance criteria before release.
 Test Sadie across real-world scenarios to ensure features and behaviours work as intended.
 Review real customer calls, feedback, and product usage to identify gaps, edge cases, and opportunities for improvement.
 Work with customers and internal teams to understand problems and translate feedback into actionable product requirements.
 Coordinate product pilots and releases, including defining scope, expected behaviour, success criteria, and feedback loops.
 Identify dependencies, blockers, risks, and missing requirements before they impact delivery.
 Maintain clear documentation around product functionality, decisions, requirements, and expected behaviour.
 Track progress against the roadmap and communicate product status, blockers, and changes to relevant stakeholders.
 Ensure features are not simply shipped, but actually fulfil the original product vision and solve the intended customer problem.
 Continuously improve how requirements are defined, communicated, tested, and delivered across the product organization.
 What You Bring 
 2+ years of experience as a Product Owner, Business Analyst, or similar product-focused role.
 Experience working closely with software engineering teams to deliver customer-facing products.
 Strong ability to take a high-level product idea and turn it into detailed, actionable requirements.
 Experience writing clear product tickets, user stories, acceptance criteria, and functional requirements.
 Strong understanding of product workflows, user journeys, edge cases, and expected system behaviours.
 Experience managing and prioritizing a product backlog.
 Strong attention to detail and the ability to identify gaps or ambiguity before development begins.
 Ability to understand technical concepts sufficiently to communicate effectively with engineering teams.
 Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to make pragmatic decisions when requirements or priorities change.
 Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
 Ability to manage multiple initiatives and priorities in a fast-moving environment.
 Strong sense of ownership and accountability for the quality of the final product, not just the completion of tickets.
 Pluses 
 Experience working on conversational, voice, communications, or workflow products.
 Experience working with hospitality, restaurants, hotels, or other service-based businesses.
 Experience managing complex products with multiple integrations and dependencies.
 Experience working in a startup or fast-moving product environment.
 Comfortable working in an environment where the roadmap evolves quickly based on customer and business needs.
 Am I Right for This Position? 
 You will be a strong fit if you enjoy taking an idea that may initially be high-level or ambiguous and turning it into something an engineering team can confidently build.
 You should naturally think about questions like:
 What exactly should happen? What happens if something goes wrong? What are the edge cases? What does success look like? Does what we built actually match what we intended?
 You do not need to be an engineer. You do need to be comfortable working closely with engineers and taking ownership of the detail required to turn a product vision into a working product.
 Why Is This Job Important? 
 Sadie is evolving quickly, and our ability to execute on our product vision depends on turning ideas and customer needs into clear, well-defined work for our engineering teams.
 The Product Owner sits between vision and execution.
 Your responsibility is to make sure the roadmap does not remain a collection of ideas. It becomes clearly defined functionality that engineering can build, customers can use, and the business can measure.
 What Will I Learn in This Position? 
 You will gain hands-on experience building and scaling a rapidly evolving technology product used in real customer interactions every day.
 You will work closely with leadership, engineering, customers, and commercial teams and develop a deep understanding of how product strategy is translated into requirements, delivered through engineering, validated with customers, and continuously improved.

The Staff Product Manager is an Individual Contributor (IC) product leader responsible for a broad platform surface for Atlas Infinite at MongoDB. Atlas Infinite is the largest architectural innovation in MongoDB Atlas ever, purpose-built to handle today's speed and scale of development and demand. 
 In this position, you will own and solve end-to-end problems around the user experience and database experience of Atlas Infinite, including but limited to feature discovery, activation, monetization, and retention. You will see patterns, opportunities, and risks across areas, own cross-team product and architectural trade-offs, establish reusable standards for PM craft, and align senior stakeholders around multi-year bets. You have deep knowledge of cloud database platforms, distributed data systems, and enterprise product development.
 You will partner closely with cross-functional engineering leaders, product peers, and executive stakeholders to drive outcomes across organizational boundaries, guiding a portfolio spanning Atlas Infinite's disaggregated compute and storage architecture, production workload readiness, migration and Atlas interoperability, and the new customer experiences this architecture may make possible. You will not inherit a closed list of future features: part of your mandate is to discover opportunities we have not yet articulated and challenge assumptions about which problems matter most. With AWS public preview now live, you will help turn real workload evidence into a credible path to GA and subsequent releases, in close partnership with the existing team.
 This role can be based out of a MongoDB office or remotely in Canada.
 Responsibilities
 Interlinked Vision & Multi-Year Bets: Set and champion a product vision across Atlas Infinite's capabilities, while actively discovering opportunities that are not on today's roadmap or fit any single team's remit. Explore what decoupled compute and storage could make possible for developers, enterprises, and emerging AI workloads; use hypotheses, customer evidence, prototypes, and market signals to uncover needs we have not yet named. Branching, on-demand compute, and instant recovery are examples of possible bets. Make the case for investment and prioritization, including build-vs-buy considerations, and distinguish exploratory vision from release commitments
 Cross-Team Execution: Along with program management, own execution health across workstreams, negotiating sequencing, scope, and resource trade-offs with engineering leaders and peer PMs where you have no direct authority. Ensure preview-to-GA readiness, roadmaps, and dependencies across database, storage, Atlas platform, migration, backup, security, and cloud infrastructure teams are aligned and connect to company objectives
 Execution & Research Standards: Establish lightweight operating practices and shared customer/market research frameworks that make workload qualification, customer-representative testing, win/loss analysis, launch readiness, and post-launch learning consistent across the portfolio. Use data to drive decisions without overburdening delivery teams
 Product Health: Resolve complex post-launch escalations when the root cause spans architecture, performance, migration, observability, supportability, or unclear ownership. Turn customer and operational signals into systemic product fixes rather than one-off workarounds
 Customer Discovery: Identify needs and competitive dynamics that cut across product areas. Look beyond requests from today's customers to discover emerging jobs-to-be-done, surprising uses of the architecture, and reasons customers do not choose MongoDB at all. Combine interviews, workload and pricing evidence, product analytics, field feedback, and experiments to test known hypotheses and uncover unknowns; reorient the roadmap when the evidence warrants it
 Outbound & GTM: Partner with product marketing, pricing, sales, solutions architecture, customer success, documentation, and support on high-stakes customer engagements, product positioning, and omni-channel marketing. Establish ideal customer profile; ensure claims and migration guidance match demonstrated capabilities; translate successful adoption and enablement approaches into shared playbooks
 Executive Alignment: Synthesize customer experience, technical readiness, adoption, and commercial impact into clear, confident product stories for senior leadership. Surface cross-area risks and progress early, including trade-offs between new-workload growth, customer savings, and changes to existing Atlas usage
 Mentorship: Mentor PMs across the area, sharing frameworks for cross-team alignment, customer evidence, technical trade-offs, multi-year bets, and leadership communication
 Qualifications
 8+ years of product management or equivalent product leadership experience, with a track record personally shaping strategy and outcomes for complex technical platforms across multiple teams, rather than only coordinating delivery
 Strong technical fluency in cloud databases, distributed data systems, storage infrastructure, developer experiences, or an adjacent developer platform. Able to reason with engineers about architecture, performance, availability, data movement, and trade-offs without needing to be the system designer
 A demonstrated ability to discover opportunities beyond the current roadmap: connect technical possibilities to unmet customer needs, formulate and test hypotheses, notice surprising patterns, and change direction when evidence challenges the original thesis
 Experience taking a complex product from early adoption toward dependable, broader use while protecting space for longer-term innovation; able to make explicit trade-offs among customer trust, technical readiness, speed, and investment
 Proven ability to influence without authority, negotiating sequencing and resource trade-offs across partner teams with competing priorities

 KittySpout is a premium DTC brand selling stainless steel cat water fountains, filters, and accessories. What is our culture like & who is a good fit? 
 Culture-fit is our #1 factor when hiring! We have a genuine will-to-win. No work is beneath us if it moves us towards our goals. We utilize creativity to do more with less - and quickly. We use data to make decisions and live by the following three core values: work smart, overdeliver, speed is king, and better everyday. We love learning - every problem is an opportunity to grow.

 Manage the full creative process (from scripting all the way to final creative) in order to produce high converting creatives on an ongoing basis.
 Drive measurable improvements in core advertising metrics across digital channels with improved creatives.
 Script Direct response creatives

 Work with our marketing team to come up with new creative concepts and ideas.
 Conduct strategic customer and competitor research to better optimize creative efforts
 Provide creative reports on a monthly and quarterly basis
 Decide on the next steps needed to scale Meta Ads further through better creative
 Produce a minimum of 15 ad briefs per week , maintaining volume and quality simultaneously — without being chased.
 Fully remote
 Fluent in English

 Strong analytical skills with hands-on experience interpreting performance data from platforms such as Northbeam, Facebook Ads, leveraging spreadsheets and reporting tools to extract insights, inform strategy and communicate campaign ideas and results.

 Excellent cultural fit as per our values above.
 Are excited to play a big role in scaling the company and work closely with the founders.
 Proven VSL copywriting experience on DR / performance brands
 Deep DTC Experience: You can name the brands and the spend levels behind your work — not just categories.
 Meta VSLs: Proven experience with both short and long form Meta VSLs. Long form is the bulk of what we run.

 Deep fluency with DTC and modern consumer brands

 If you want a stress-free corporate 9-5 job, this isn't it.

 Work with our marketing team to come up with new creative concepts and ideas.
 Conduct strategic customer and competitor research to better optimize creative efforts
 Provide creative reports on a monthly and quarterly basis
 Decide on the next steps needed to scale Meta Ads further through better creative
 Produce a minimum of 15 ad briefs per week , maintaining volume and quality simultaneously — without being chased.

 Fluent in English

 Deep fluency with DTC and modern consumer brands

DO YOU WANT TO IMPACT THE HARDEST WORKING PEOPLE IN THE WORLD?

Then Jobber might be the place for you! We’re looking for a Senior Lifecycle Marketing Manager to be part of our Marketing department.



Jobber exists to help people in small businesses be successful. We work with small home service businesses, like your local plumbers, painters, and landscapers, to transform the way service is delivered through technology. With Jobber they can quote, schedule, invoice, and collect payments from their customers while providing an easy and professional customer experience. Running a small business today isn’t like it used to be—the way we consume and deliver service is changing rapidly, technology is evolving, and customers expect more. That’s why we put the power and flexibility in their hands to run their businesses how, where, and when they want!

Our culture of transparency, inclusivity, collaboration, and innovation has been recognized by Great Place to Work, Canada’s Most Admired Corporate Cultures, and more. Jobber has also been named on the Globe and Mail’s Canada’s Top Growing Companies list, and Deloitte Canada’s Technology Fast 50™, Enterprise Fast 15, and Technology Fast 500™ lists. With an Executive team that has over thirty years of industry experience of leading the way, we’ve come a long way from our first customer in 2011—but we’ve just scratched the surface of what we want to accomplish for our customers https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EkfZmHrRLx4&list=PLoktA_D-2UEnxMLfCe93bANKXVXd2bdN8&index=25.



The Team:

When it comes to telling the world about Jobber and moving new people through a funnel, Marketing is your department. They handle everything from spreading awareness, to answering “What’s Jobber?,” to getting new customers in the door, to turning those customers into Jobber advocates!

Lifecycle marketing is responsible for creating and advocating for best-in-class experiences that deliver the right message, to the right people, at the right time. We leverage automation and data to build highly personalized end-to-end experiences our customers want, need, and like.



The Role:

Reporting to the Acquisition Manager,  Lifecycle Marketing, the Senior Lifecycle Marketing Manager will be responsible for orchestrating our ideal customer experience. You will own and drive strategies for how we acquire, activate, retain, and expand users on all platforms. You will be accountable for enhancing our Lead Nurture efforts and creating experiences that are mutually beneficial to both customers and Jobber, ultimately ensuring we’re effectively capturing revenue.

You will partner cross-functionally to optimize our customer journey, including all associated customer communications. In addition, you will run experiments to explore and validate new strategies for how we can effectively move our customers through the funnel. You will represent Lifecycle Marketing across the organization and be a steward for your area of focus across the business.

Through your work with our Business Operations, Marketing, Sales, Success, Product, and Growth teams, you'll create great user experiences at scale and conduct experiments to discover what works.



The Senior Lifecycle Marketing Manager will:

 - Own the Leads portfolio end to end: the strategy, the programs, and the metrics for how leads are nurtured into trials and how trials convert into paying customers.

 - Own and extend Jobber’s AI-enriched lead journeys, using enrichment and orchestration tooling (currently Clay and n8n) to build customer profiles and route leads into personalized experiences based on intent.

 - Connect the lead experience to the trial experience so a customer sees one continuous, personalized journey from first touch through conversion, and work with Product on how that personalization carries into the app.

 - Run a test-and-learn program against lead-to-trial and trial-to-paid metrics: form hypotheses, design experiments, read the results honestly, and iterate until the number moves.

 - Decide where the portfolio’s time goes. Diagnose where leads and trials are being lost, size the opportunities, and make the case for what comes first and what waits.

 - Lead the acquisition pod that connects lifecycle with our outbound and demand generation partners, owning the plan and the handoffs between teams and keeping leadership informed.

 - Build what you design. Depending on capacity, you’ll configure journeys, write emails, and set up automation yourself alongside our Revenue Communications team.

 - Set the bar for the Lifecycle team: bring outside insight in, share what you learn, and raise how the practice works at Jobber.



To be successful, you should:

 - Have deep experience owning lead nurture and trial-to-paid conversion programs at a SaaS company, with results you can point to. B2B SaaS is the closest fit.

 - Have hands-on experience using AI tools to enrich customer data and personalize communications at scale, beyond drafting copy. You’ve built or configured enrichment, orchestration, or journey logic yourself and can say what it changed in your results.

 - Bring a test-and-learn posture to AI: you experiment with new tooling in your own workflow, can separate what works from what’s hype, and are comfortable in the weeds when the data is incomplete.

 - Have led integrated acquisition efforts across outbound, demand generation, product, and sales, owning the plan and the handoffs rather than executing the lifecycle piece of someone else’s.

 - Know the metrics behind nurture and conversion cold, and have moved them through experimentation and program iteration, not just reported on them.

 - Take full ownership of the outcomes tied to your KPIs, including when the data is imperfect. You find a way to measure, ship, and learn rather than wait for clean inputs.

 - Understand customer behaviour, barriers, and motivations from first-hand sources, and change the journey because of what you learn.

 - Operate with a high degree of autonomy. You set your own priorities, keep your manager informed without being asked, and flag risk early.

 - Push for better ways of doing things, and stay humble while you do it.



Location:

We believe great collaboration is intentional, and sometimes that means coming together in person to build, brainstorm, and connect. To support this, the role is open to candidates based in one of our hub cities: Edmonton, Toronto, Vancouver, or Kitchener-Waterloo.



Compensation:

At Jobber, we believe that compensation should be transparent, fair, and reflective of your experience and growth. This role has a minimum annual salary of $99,540, a midpoint of $142,200, and a maximum salary of $163,530, designed to show the progression from learning the ropes to truly excelling.

We design our compensation to reflect each new hire’s skills, experience against the complexity of the role, ensuring a fair and competitive salary. Our range is intentionally broad to support growth and long-term impact, with fully established hires typically starting around the midpoint. The higher end of the range is reserved for those who have demonstrated deep expertise and lasting contributions, while offers below the midpoint reflect strong potential with room to develop. This approach ensures that compensation aligns with both an individual’s current capabilities and their opportunity for future growth.

Base salary is just one part of a total compensation package that will include equity rewards, annual stipends for health and wellness, retirement savings matching, and an extended health package with fully paid premiums for body and mind. Your professional growth matters to us too! You’ll have access to a dedicated talent development program that includes career coaching and opportunities for career development.

We believe in transparency and open conversations about compensation. If you have any questions about our approach, we’re happy to discuss them throughout the hiring process!

What you can expect from Jobber:

 - A total compensation package that includes an extended health benefits package with fully paid premiums for both body and mind, matching in RRSP, TFSA or FHSA, and stock options.

 - A dedicated Talent Development team and access to coaching, learning, and leadership programs to help you grow your career, reach your goals, and unlock your full potential.

 - A unique opportunity to build, grow, and leave your impact on a $400-billion industry that has no dominant player...yet.

 - To work with a group of people who are humble, supportive, and give a sh*t about our customers.

We believe that diverse teams perform better and that fostering an inclusive work environment is a key part of growing a successful team. We welcome people of diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we are committed to working with applicants requesting accommodation at any stage of the hiring process.



A bit more about us:

Job by job, we’re transforming the way service is delivered. Your lawn care provider, home cleaning service, plumber or painter could use Jobber to better connect with their customers, save time in the office, invoice faster, and get paid! We’re bringing tens of thousands of people together with technology to deliver billions of dollars a year in services to happy customers. Jobber exists to help make these small businesses successful, and when they’re successful we all win!

A little about Capital Power 
 Capital Power (TSX: CPX) is dedicated to  Powering Change by Changing Power . This north star guides our ambitions, focus, and actions as we transform our energy system. We're a growth-oriented North American energy company headquartered in Edmonton, Alberta. Our team safely delivers, builds, and creates balanced energy solutions for customers across North America.

With us, your contributions matter – we want you to be empowered to innovate, collaborate, and ultimately drive results. We're here to partner with you so you can learn, grow, and forge a career that's meaningful to you. Join us in powering North America!
 Your Opportunity 
 One Permanent Full Time Position  
 The Senior Specialist, Market Risk role, within Capital Power’s middle office, provides independent analysis and oversight of market risk exposures across power, natural gas, and environmental portfolios. The role evaluates trading and hedging strategies, governs price curves and valuation methodologies, and develops and executes market risk analytics including VaR, stress testing, scenario analysis, and assessment of non‑linear exposures.
 The position supports new product approvals and complex structured transactions through development and validation of valuation methods, risk models, and exposures, and monitors risk limits and escalation processes. Through strong model validation, analytical insight, and risk reporting, the role delivers clear, defensible risk insights to support effective decision‑making and the continued development of the Market Risk function.
 As part of a rapidly growing team, the successful candidate will demonstrate flexibility and a desire to contribute to wider team growth and development.
 You will contribute to our team by: 
 • Strategy analysis: Prospectively analyze and validate trading and hedging strategies proposed by Front Office to ensure consistency with approved risk management objectives and the firm’s risk profile.
 • Valuation and curve oversight: Ensure appropriate price curves and valuation methodologies are in place for all new deals, strategies, and structured transactions; validate valuation and exposures of proposed structured transactions and prepare supporting risk analysis as required.
 • Hedge effectiveness analysis: Perform periodic retrospective analysis to assess the effectiveness of authorized hedging strategies and evaluate whether intended risk management outcomes are being achieved.
 • Risk quantification and analytics: Develop, maintain, and execute market risk analytics, including Value‑at‑Risk, stress testing, back‑testing, scenario analysis, sensitivities, and assessment of non‑linear portfolio exposures.
 • Risk limit monitoring: Execute an ongoing process to review portfolio exposures against approved market risk limits, investigate and escalate breaches, and produce exception reporting.
 • Model development and validation: Develop and validate pricing and risk methodologies for new, complex, or illiquid instruments (including mark‑to‑model approaches), and generation and storage assets; provide ongoing governance and independent validation of valuation and risk models, inputs, and assumptions.

 Education

 Experience

 • Experience developing and validating pricing and risk models.

 • Familiarity with risk management of generation and storage assets.
 Technical Skills

Citylitics delivers predictive intelligence on where, how, and why infrastructure investments will occur across North America.
 Infrastructure includes the foundational systems that shape our quality of life: water, transportation, transit, roads and highways, broadband, and power. It represents a multi-trillion-dollar market and a 20+ year megatrend in North America.
 Citylitics transforms millions of documents across more than 40,000 cities, utilities, and public agencies into real-time market signals and high-value sales intelligence. Leading infrastructure vendors, engineering firms, and construction companies use the platform to identify and pre-position for major infrastructure opportunities earlier, helping them build relationships, shape project priorities, and influence scope before projects move to formal procurement. 
 Citylitics combines a network of AI agents, fine-tuned models, a proprietary infrastructure signals graph, and daily human-in-the-loop quality assurance workflows to deliver highly nuanced and reliable sales intelligence. The platform integrates seamlessly with CRMs, ERPs, and data lakes, embedding actionable insights directly into sales workflows so teams can prioritize the right pursuits and build stronger pipelines.
 Our mission is to improve how infrastructure investments get made so critical needs can be addressed earlier and communities benefit from stronger, more resilient infrastructure.
 Join Citylitics to work in a meaningful industry that will matter for decades to come while helping grow a company at the forefront of applied AI. We operate with a Results-Driven Mentality and a commitment to Raise The Bar, in a collaborative environment where Teamwork Makes the Dream Work as we tackle big challenges and celebrate wins together.
 Who Are We Looking For? 
 We're looking for a skilled and enthusiastic Data Engineer to join our growing team! We're a close-knit group building and maintaining mission-critical data products, and we need someone who can hit the ground running.
 This role requires a strong command of data engineering best practices, a track record with orchestration and data warehouses, and hands-on experience shipping LLM and agentic workflows to production. You'll own the design, build, and operation of production data pipelines that use AI to power customer-facing solutions. You'll work with technologies we already use, including GCP services like Cloud Composer, Cloud SQL, BigQuery, and Vertex AI.
 Beyond the technical skills, we value collaboration, sound engineering judgment, and the ability to adapt as AI tooling changes fast. If you're passionate about data, have put AI into production and want to do more of it, and are excited by impactful projects, we encourage you to apply.
 This is a hybrid role based out of Citylitics’ Toronto office and requires 3+ days in-office per week. 
 What Will You Accomplish? / How You Will Make An Immediate Impact: 
 Pipeline Orchestration: Lead the development of highly performant, reliable, and maintainable pipelines using Airflow and BigQuery, from architecture and design through testing, deployment, monitoring, and maintenance. You'll make design decisions independently and own the systems you build.
 Data Modeling & Dashboards: Partner with data analysts and stakeholders to define requirements and design scalable data models and applications. You'll own data products end to end, from the pipelines and models through the backend APIs to the customer-facing dashboards and apps built on them.
 AI & Agentic Workflows: Design and operate pipelines that use LLMs and agents to turn raw documents into structured, useful data. This includes prompt and context design, tool and function calling, embeddings and retrieval, structured outputs, and production concerns like retries, idempotency, cost, and latency. You'll also own evaluation datasets, LLM-as-judge and rule-based QA checks, and benchmarks that turn results into clear decisions about models, prompts, and architecture.
 Continuous Improvement: Drive the ongoing improvement of our data infrastructure and processes, including evaluating and introducing new technologies and best practices.  Proficiency in Python and SQL.
 Proven experience (3+ years) working as a Data Engineer or Software Engineer in a cloud environment.
 Experience building production data pipelines with an orchestrator like Airflow/Cloud Composer and a data warehouse like BigQuery.
 Solid grasp of data engineering fundamentals: data modeling, ETL/ELT, and building idempotent, reliable pipelines.
 Experience shipping LLM-powered features or pipelines to production with LLM APIs (e.g., Gemini, Claude, OpenAI): prompting, structured outputs, and tool/function calling.

 Daily, fluent use of AI coding agents (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor) in your workflow, with the judgment to review and verify what they produce.
 Experience with Git, CI/CD, and cloud platforms (GCP preferred).

 Excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to work independently on ambiguous problems.
 Excellent communication and collaboration skills. You'll be working closely with analysts, product, and other stakeholders.

At Giant Tiger, our mission is simple: help Canadians save more every day. We’re a Canadian institution rooted in our communities and built on 60+ years of success. Every item you pick, scan, pack, and ship safely plays a role in getting the right products to our stores and into the hands of Canadians who rely on us.
We’re looking for team members who are motivated, reliable, and ready to contribute to meaningful work every day. If you’re looking for hands-on work in a supportive, safety-focused environment, this opportunity is for you. This posting represents a current opportunity at Giant Tiger.
 Job Title 
Order Picker (Day Shift) 
 About This Role: 
 Giant Tiger Wholesale is looking to hire a permanent  Warehouse Order Picker  for our 660,000 square foot distribution centre in Johnstown, Ontario! 
 Do you want to learn more about what a career looks like with Giant Tiger Wholesale? Paste this link in your browser and check out our video here:  https://youtu.be/fdz66L7FBgU  
 What You’ll Be Doing: 
 Pick orders to supply over 270 Giant Tiger stores across Canada with their inventory 
 Pile various sized boxes onto skids ensuring safe, secure, and accurate piles 
 Lift boxes repeatedly with a weight range of 1-50 pounds while maintaining strict Health and Safety guidelines 
 Drive an electric double pallet truck around the warehouse to fulfill orders with a focus on safe and efficient operation 
 Identify and match picked skids with outbound license plate numbers (OLPNs) provided with the order 
 Certify accuracy for all picked inventory and ensure orders are ready for shipment within set deadlines 
 Maintain a clean, neat, and orderly work area 
 Support other departments as directed by the supervisor 
 What You'll Bring:  
 Conduct operations in a manner which promotes safety and complies with Ontario Safety and Health Act (OSHA), and Workplace Hazardous Materials Information System (WHMIS) standards 
 Capable of standing, walking, climbing stairs and repetitively lifting heavy objects throughout shift 
 Comfortable in a noisy, fast-paced environment 
 Punctual, adaptable, and strong attention to detail 
 Able to maintain a professional appearance and demeanor 
 As part of your onboarding, you will be required to complete three days of paid machine training and successfully obtain in-house certification. Successful machine certification is a mandatory condition of employment as it is an occupational requirement.  
 Assets You May Have:  
 Experience with Voice Picking or Manhattan Warehouse Management System 
 Experience driving an electric double pallet truck or similar machine 
 Experience in a warehouse environment 
 Class G2 or higher driver’s license 
 When You'll Work:  
 Sunday - Wednesday, 6:30am - 5:00pm
 Giant Tiger is proud to offer a Total Rewards package designed to support your financial security, health, and career growth. This includes competitive compensation for all employees, as well as retirement savings support and comprehensive well-being benefits for our permanent team members.

$20.48

 Competitive Compensation : The expected pay rate for this position is listed above, and Giant Tiger offers guaranteed increases based on cumulative hours worked.  Retirement Support : We automatically contribute 6% of your annual earnings to a Deferred Profit Sharing Plan account for you, fully funded by the company for all permanent, full-time employees.

Campaign Conductor: You’re a strategic marketing leader who knows how to turn a campaign from a loose idea into a fully coordinated revenue machine. You’ve planned offers, mapped customer journeys, briefed channels, aligned stakeholders, watched the numbers, and made smart optimizations when performance demanded it. Fluent in the full funnel, you know paid media, ecommerce, email, loyalty, creative, customer service, and analytics all need to work together — or the customer feels the cracks. If that sounds like you, here’s your next big opportunity:
 AlgaeCal is searching for a top-tier Marketing Leader (Campaigns) to join our team and propel our revenue growth to new heights.
 Small print here ⇒ We’re an eCommerce company. So, we want you to have eCommerce experience. Lots of it. So if you don’t love digital marketing the way cats love cream, you probably shouldn’t read any further. 
 Still here? Okay then…
 This job will give you ALL the feels:
 At AlgaeCal, we’re driven by a single idea. To end the fear of bone loss. In the United States, an estimated 54 million people have low bone density. 
 The good news? AlgaeCal has the world’s only clinically-backed natural solution to this problem. We give hope to everyone worried about bone loss. If that excites you, you’ll find no better place to continue your career than at AlgaeCal. 
 This job might be for you if you’ve got…
 2+ years of marketing leadership experience planning and executing D2C campaigns in an eCommerce environment. You’ve led campaigns from the first messy idea through briefing, approvals, launch, optimization, reporting, and “okay, what did we learn?” You know campaigns don’t magically happen because someone made a promo calendar. They happen because someone owns the moving parts.
 A track record of managing six-figure monthly marketing budgets. You've worked with substantial media investments, understand how budget allocation impacts overall business performance, and know that maximizing profit matters more than simply maximizing spend.
 A Yoda-like ability to make strategic, data-driven decisions. When we look at your resume, we’ll see proof that you know how to turn campaign performance data into smart decisions. CPA, ROAS, revenue, customer segments, contribution margin, EBITDA - these numbers don’t make your eyes glaze over. They make your brain start whirring.
 A full-funnel brain that sees the whole customer journey. Paid media, email, ecommerce, loyalty, organic social, affiliates, influencers, customer service, marketplaces - you understand these channels don’t live in separate little kingdoms. They all touch the same customer. And if the journey feels disjointed, confusing, repetitive, or poorly timed, performance suffers.
 Strategy that converts like a tent revival. You’ve planned campaigns that engage, educate, and motivate people to take action. You understand offer strategy, timing, landing pages, upsells, cross-sells, bundles, coupons, discount logic, and the tiny campaign mechanics that can quietly make or break revenue. You know when evergreen ads, emails, popups, organic posts, or automations need to pause, shift, suppress, or get out of the way so a live campaign can do its job.
 A brain the size of a small planet! In this role, you’ll need to think imaginatively and act strategically. You’ll balance company priorities, finance approvals, product logistics, creative capacity, compliance, customer service needs, and channel constraints without melting into a puddle.
 A results-driven approach to paid media and campaign budget. You’ve worked closely with Paid Media teams, helped allocate spend across campaigns, and know how to look beyond surface-level ROAS. Revenue is nice. Profitability is nicer. You understand unit economics, contribution margin, and why a campaign can look good in one dashboard and less thrilling in another.
 A track record of leadership, mentorship, and cross-functional coordination. You’ve worked with channel owners, project managers, analysts, creatives, and senior leaders to get campaigns out the door without everyone needing therapy afterward. You guide, influence, pitch, negotiate, and push back when needed - without turning into a tiny workplace dictator.
 The ability to put on the Customer Hat at all times. You think through what a new prospect sees, what a returning customer receives, how reward points affect the offer, what happens if someone talks to Customer Service, and whether the whole experience actually makes sense to a real human being.
 Experience designing and executing customer journeys. From first click to final purchase, from campaign email to landing page, from retargeting ad to checkout, from BAU content to live promo, you know how to make every touchpoint feel connected, intentional, and easy to follow.
 A thick portfolio that demonstrates your mastery of all-things eCommerce. Sorry, but if you have to Google what a heatmap is, don’t know why site speed matters, or think an A/B test is just “trying a different headline,” this probably isn’t the job for you.
 A detective’s eye for revenue leakage. Coupon abuse, conflicting emails, poorly timed popups, expired offers, unclear bundles, bad suppression logic, clunky checkout journeys, ads running to the wrong page - you can spot the problems before they quietly drain sales.
 An encyclopedic knowledge of today’s martech, adtech, attribution, and analytics landscape. You don’t blindly trust one dashboard because it has a pretty graph. You understand tools like Triple Whale and GA4 can disagree, and you know how to contextualize performance instead of taking any single source as gospel.
 A strong grasp of testing strategy. A/B testing, multivariate testing, UX tests, offer tests, funnel tests, creative tests - you know how to plan tests that align with bigger roadmaps instead of throwing spaghetti at a wall and calling it “experimentation.”
 A solid understanding of UI/UX. This isn’t essential, but it’s a definite plus. You don’t need to be a designer, but you should understand how UX and UI choices affect customer behavior, conversion, trust, and campaign performance. And yes, we might swoon if you have it.
 A healthy respect for compliance, claims, and disclaimers. We work in the health space, which means “close enough” is not close enough. You’ll need to understand marketing claims, product basics, customer service considerations, and legal disclaimers well enough to keep campaigns accurate, compliant, and trustworthy.
 Now, time to be honest: is this really you? If you’re nodding your head and feeling that flutter of excitement, then we can’t wait to meet you.
 Other Qualities You’ll Need 
 At AlgaeCal, we’re going to insist that you have these 3 qualities:
 You’re humble–you put the team and others’ needs ahead of your own
 You’re hungry to learn more
 You’re people smart–in the sense that you’re a great teammate
 The truth is, if you don’t have these qualities, you won’t last long at AlgaeCal. So if you’re missing one of them, be honest. Save yourself a lot of headaches and skip to a job posting that is a better fit for you.
 What Will You Earn?  
 We believe in rewarding top talent. So let’s talk about salary once we’ve had the chance to get to know you better. Rest assured, we’re generous and offer above-market pay for the right person. If you bring the skills and experience, we’ll make sure the compensation reflects that.
 You’ll also enjoy the following benefits: 
 A generous healthcare package
 Monthly team events and activities
 Flexible Stat Holidays with the option to bank days for later use
 Weekly team lunches
 Casual dress code
 Incredible dog-friendly, Yaletown office one block from SkyTrain
 Remote working is okay with us too.
 And above all, you’ll join a team that you’ll never want to leave. Culture is everything to us. Yes, we work extremely hard to change as many people’s lives as possible. But we know how to have fun and reward ourselves too.
 How To Apply 
 So, do you have what it takes to become the next member of team AlgaeCal?
 Job opportunities like this don’t come along often, and we’ve got a lot to offer our successful applicant. So, to make sure our future Marketing Leader (Campaigns) Lead is the real deal, will be a great fit, and will thrive at AlgaeCal, we ask a little more than your run-of-the-mill job application:
 If this sounds like a position for you, please respond to this advertisement with your resume and cover letter. Please, read carefully:
 1. Write a cover letter addressing: 
 Why are you the best Marketing Leader (Campaigns) for this role? Give quantifiable examples of related achievements.
 Describe why you fit perfectly with our values. Read them here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1deCCJZ6tiDiOSlr_W0UdCuM_V_ahzPBs/view 
 What's the toughest challenge you’ve ever overcome in your life? How did you overcome it?
 What are the last three books you’ve read?
 What do you do for fun?
 2. Explain what you’re doing now for a job: 
  If you don’t have one, explain why.
  If you have one, explain why you’re looking elsewhere.
 3. Upload your cover letter and resume 
 Ensure that your cover letter and resume are saved and sent as one file.
 Yes, our hiring process is challenging, but it’s our way of selecting the best–and your way of ensuring your AlgaeCal teammates are tops.
 Click the “Apply Now” button on this page and upload your cover letter and resume. 
 ***Note: Please include your cover letter WITH your resume in one document. Applications without a cover letter will not be read!** *
 We are looking to hire as soon as we find the right person, so act quickly, and you can also expect a prompt response.

 AI Strategy & Roadmap 
 ·         Own the Corporate IT AI strategy and roadmap, aligned with CIO and enterprise priorities.
 ·         Lead intake, value assessment and prioritization of AI use cases across functions such as Actuarial, Risk, Compliance, Human Resources, Finance, Legal, Procurement etc.

 ·         Define AI patterns and align them with Enterprise Architecture standards.

 Security, Risk & Responsible AI

 ·         Protect AI solutions against data leakage, prompt injection and model abuse.
 ·         Partner with Risk, Legal, Compliance and Privacy to establish and operate AI controls.
 ·         Support privacy, SOX, model-risk and audit requirements for AI-enabled corporate processes.
 ·         Maintain an accurate inventory of AI solutions and an approved-tools catalogue.
 People, Talent & Adoption 
 ·         Lead AI engineering, platform and automation teams and establish clear accountabilities.
 ·         Design roles, career paths and team structures that build sustainable AI capability within Corporate IT.
 ·         Mentor IT employees in AI engineering and secure, responsible AI practices.
 ·         Drive employee AI adoption and literacy in partnership with corporate function owners.
 ·         Manage strategic partners and managed service providers and hold them accountable for outcomes.
 IT Service Delivery & Operations 
 ·         Deliver AI initiatives through established portfolio, change, release and governance processes.
 ·         Own service-level expectations, support models, runbooks and operational readiness for AI services.
 ·         Partner with corporate function owners to define outcomes and realize measurable value.
 ·         Report value, risk, delivery and spend to the CIO and IT leadership.
 ·         Lead change management and communications for AI rollouts.
 What do you need to succeed? 
 ·         Demonstrated hands-on experience building and delivering artificial intelligence or machine learning solutions into production, supported by a strong foundation in software engineering, data engineering or machine learning.
 ·         Experience designing AI engineering patterns and guiding engineering teams through technical implementation while remaining actively involved in solution development.
 ·         Proficiency with Python and experience with data integration, data pipelines or extract, transform and load processes.
 ·         Experience with cloud AI services and application programming interfaces on Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure or both.

 ·         Experience navigating information security, data protection, responsible AI and technology-governance requirements in a complex enterprise environment.
 ·         Ability to explain complex technical recommendations to engineering teams, senior leaders and business stakeholders, mentor colleagues and build alignment across teams.
 ·         Experience working in a regulated or highly governed enterprise environment.

 ·         Degree or advanced education in computer science, software engineering, data science, machine learning or a related discipline, or equivalent work experience.
 What's in it for you?

 Job Description 
 Conseiller Technique de Chantier (Turbine et Alternateur)/ Site Technical Advisor (Turbine and Generator) 
 Introduction au rôle 
 L’Aviseur Technique Chantier (Turbine et Alternateur) est le spécialiste technique présent sur site, chargé de soutenir les activités d’installation et de mise en service des projets hydroélectriques. Il veille à ce que les travaux mécaniques et l’ensemble des travaux soient exécutés conformément aux études de conception, aux normes techniques, aux exigences qualité ainsi qu’aux réglementations en matière de santé, sécurité et environnement.
 Responsabilités principales 
 Santé, Sécurité et Environnement (SSE) : 
 Assurer la conformité SSE, évaluer les tâches afin d’identifier les dangers et vérifier que les mesures de contrôle préviennent les blessures et les incidents. Arrêter les travaux si les risques ne sont pas maîtrisés.
 Promouvoir une forte culture sécurité et veiller à ce que tous les travaux techniques respectent les exigences SSE.
 Participer aux analyses de risques, aux modes opératoires et aux analyses de sécurité pour les activités à haut risque (levages lourds, espaces confinés, travaux par point chaud, en hauteur ou sous tension).
 Soutenir la mise en œuvre des mesures de protection environnementale et le respect des permis et obligations réglementaires.
 Planification et Coordination des Travaux : 
 Collaborer étroitement avec le Chef de Chantier pour planifier, séquencer et alimenter les plannings de construction des tâches techniques et du chemin critique.
 Agir en tant que point de contact technique sur site pour les ingénieurs d’études, chefs de projet, méthodes, sous-traitants et clients.
 Coordonner les sous-traitants spécialisés et participer aux réunions techniques, clarifications de conception et discussions de gestion des changements.
 Exécution Technique et Supervision :
 Fournir un support technique quotidien et une expertise aux équipes de chantier, tout en encadrant et dirigeant la main-d’œuvre dans l’exécution des activités.
 Surveiller de près les processus d’installation critiques (alignement des turbines et générateurs, installation des paliers, accouplement des arbres, levages critiques).
 Réaliser des interventions techniques qualifiées (alignement de lignes d’arbres, réglage des paliers, outils de précision, réglage d’outils d’usinage sur site).
 Examiner et interpréter les plans d’ingénierie, manuels et spécifications pour garantir la conformité aux exigences des OEM (Original Equipment Manufacturer).
  Qualité, Essais et Clôture de Projet : 
 Participer aux inspections et contrôles qualité (alignement, soudage, coulis) et signaler toute non-conformité conformément au plan qualité.
 Soutenir la résolution des non-conformités techniques et des réserves (punch list).
 Examiner et valider les résultats d’essais, contribuer à la documentation « tel que construit » (as-built) et aux dossiers de remise O&M.
 Piloter les analyses de causes racines pour les problèmes de chantier, recommander des solutions techniques et capitaliser les retours d’expérience.
 Qualifications et Compétences 
 Formation : Diplôme d’ingénieur en mécanique, électricité ou génie civil (ou discipline technique équivalente). Un diplôme technique équivalent avec une expérience significative en construction hydroélectrique ou de centrales sera également considéré.
  Expérience 
 Minimum de 5 ans d’expérience préalable sur des générateurs hydroélectriques, idéalement dans un rôle de supervision.
 Minimum de 5 ans d’expérience en installation mécanique de lignes d’arbres, turbines ou générateurs.
 Solides connaissances des systèmes et structures des centrales hydroélectriques ; capacité à lire et comprendre manuels, plans et spécifications.
  Compétences relationnelles et personnelles : 
 Aptitude avérée à diriger, motiver, responsabiliser les équipes et à travailler sous pression.
 Solides compétences en résolution de problèmes, prise de décision sur le terrain et en relations interpersonnelles.
 Excellente communication orale et écrite, et bonne maîtrise de MS Office.
 Être proactif sur les sujets de sécurité et maintenir des relations de travail efficaces avec les équipes pluridisciplinaires.
 ---
   English Version
 Role Introduction 
 The Site Technical Advisor (Turbine and Generator) serves as the dedicated on-site technical specialist responsible for supporting the installation and commissioning of hydroelectric projects. This critical role ensures that all mechanical and associated site works are executed safely, to the highest quality standards, on schedule, and within budget, while strictly adhering to design specifications and regulatory requirements.
 Responsibilities 
   Environment, Health, and Safety (EHS): 
 Ensure EHS compliance, evaluate tasks for worker hazards, and confirm controls are active. Stop work if risks are insufficiently mitigated.
 Promote a strong safety culture and ensure technical work complies with EHS requirements, including participation in risk assessments and Job Safety Analyses (JSAs) for high-risk activities (heavy lifts, confined spaces, hot work, working at heights, energized work).
 Support environmental protection measures and regulatory compliance during construction and commissioning.
 Planning and Construction Coordination: 
 Work closely with the Site Manager to plan, sequence, and provide technical inputs to construction schedules and critical path activities.
 Act as the primary on-site technical point of contact for design engineers, project managers, methods engineers, subcontractors, and customer representatives.
 Participate in technical meetings, design clarifications, change management discussions, and coordinate with specialized subcontractors.
   Technical Execution and Oversight: 
 Provide day-to-day technical guidance, expertise, and leadership to on-site construction and labor teams.
 Closely monitor critical installation processes, such as turbine/generator alignment, bearing installation, shaft coupling, and critical lifts.
 Perform skilled technical duties involving shaft line alignment, bearing settings, precision mechanical tools, measurements, and on-site machining tools.
 Review and interpret engineering drawings, manuals, and specifications to verify adherence to design, codes, standards, and OEM requirements.
   Quality, Testing, and Project Closeout: 
 Participate in inspections and critical quality checks (alignment, welding, grouting) and report any quality issues or non-conformities per the site quality plan.
 Support the resolution of technical non-conformances and punch list items.
 Review and validate test results, support the preparation of as-built documentation, and assist with O&M handover packages.
 Lead or contribute to root cause analyses for construction issues, recommend technical solutions/field changes, and capture lessons learned.
 Qualifications and Skills 
 Education: Bachelor’s degree in mechanical, electrical, or civil engineering (or a related technical discipline). An equivalent technical diploma with substantial hydro or power plant construction experience will be considered.
   Experience: 
 Minimum of 5 years of prior hydroelectric generator experience, preferably in a supervisory capacity.
 Minimum of 5 years of experience in the mechanical installation of shaft lines, turbines, or generators.
 Strong working knowledge of hydroelectric plant systems and structures; ability to read and interpret manuals, drawings, plans, and specifications.
   Interpersonal and Professional Skills 
 Demonstrated ability to lead, motivate, and empower staff while working effectively under pressure.
 Strong problem-solving, decision-making, and field-environment judgment.
 Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with good computer skills and MS Office knowledge.
 Proactive attitude toward safety and the ability to build and maintain effective working relationships across multi-disciplinary teams.
 Additional Information 
 Relocation Assistance Provided: No

Campaign Conductor: You’re a strategic marketing leader who knows how to turn a campaign from a loose idea into a fully coordinated revenue machine. You’ve planned offers, mapped customer journeys, briefed channels, aligned stakeholders, watched the numbers, and made smart optimizations when performance demanded it. Fluent in the full funnel, you know paid media, ecommerce, email, loyalty, creative, customer service, and analytics all need to work together — or the customer feels the cracks. If that sounds like you, here’s your next big opportunity:
 AlgaeCal is searching for a top-tier Marketing Leader (Campaigns) to join our team and propel our revenue growth to new heights.
 Small print here ⇒ We’re an eCommerce company. So, we want you to have eCommerce experience. Lots of it. So if you don’t love digital marketing the way cats love cream, you probably shouldn’t read any further. 
 Still here? Okay then…
 This job will give you ALL the feels:
 At AlgaeCal, we’re driven by a single idea. To end the fear of bone loss. In the United States, an estimated 54 million people have low bone density. 
 The good news? AlgaeCal has the world’s only clinically-backed natural solution to this problem. We give hope to everyone worried about bone loss. If that excites you, you’ll find no better place to continue your career than at AlgaeCal. 
 This job might be for you if you’ve got…
 2+ years of marketing leadership experience planning and executing D2C campaigns in an eCommerce environment. You’ve led campaigns from the first messy idea through briefing, approvals, launch, optimization, reporting, and “okay, what did we learn?” You know campaigns don’t magically happen because someone made a promo calendar. They happen because someone owns the moving parts.
 A track record of managing six-figure monthly marketing budgets. You've worked with substantial media investments, understand how budget allocation impacts overall business performance, and know that maximizing profit matters more than simply maximizing spend.
 A Yoda-like ability to make strategic, data-driven decisions. When we look at your resume, we’ll see proof that you know how to turn campaign performance data into smart decisions. CPA, ROAS, revenue, customer segments, contribution margin, EBITDA - these numbers don’t make your eyes glaze over. They make your brain start whirring.
 A full-funnel brain that sees the whole customer journey. Paid media, email, ecommerce, loyalty, organic social, affiliates, influencers, customer service, marketplaces - you understand these channels don’t live in separate little kingdoms. They all touch the same customer. And if the journey feels disjointed, confusing, repetitive, or poorly timed, performance suffers.
 Strategy that converts like a tent revival. You’ve planned campaigns that engage, educate, and motivate people to take action. You understand offer strategy, timing, landing pages, upsells, cross-sells, bundles, coupons, discount logic, and the tiny campaign mechanics that can quietly make or break revenue. You know when evergreen ads, emails, popups, organic posts, or automations need to pause, shift, suppress, or get out of the way so a live campaign can do its job.
 A brain the size of a small planet! In this role, you’ll need to think imaginatively and act strategically. You’ll balance company priorities, finance approvals, product logistics, creative capacity, compliance, customer service needs, and channel constraints without melting into a puddle.
 A results-driven approach to paid media and campaign budget. You’ve worked closely with Paid Media teams, helped allocate spend across campaigns, and know how to look beyond surface-level ROAS. Revenue is nice. Profitability is nicer. You understand unit economics, contribution margin, and why a campaign can look good in one dashboard and less thrilling in another.
 A track record of leadership, mentorship, and cross-functional coordination. You’ve worked with channel owners, project managers, analysts, creatives, and senior leaders to get campaigns out the door without everyone needing therapy afterward. You guide, influence, pitch, negotiate, and push back when needed - without turning into a tiny workplace dictator.
 The ability to put on the Customer Hat at all times. You think through what a new prospect sees, what a returning customer receives, how reward points affect the offer, what happens if someone talks to Customer Service, and whether the whole experience actually makes sense to a real human being.
 Experience designing and executing customer journeys. From first click to final purchase, from campaign email to landing page, from retargeting ad to checkout, from BAU content to live promo, you know how to make every touchpoint feel connected, intentional, and easy to follow.
 A thick portfolio that demonstrates your mastery of all-things eCommerce. Sorry, but if you have to Google what a heatmap is, don’t know why site speed matters, or think an A/B test is just “trying a different headline,” this probably isn’t the job for you.
 A detective’s eye for revenue leakage. Coupon abuse, conflicting emails, poorly timed popups, expired offers, unclear bundles, bad suppression logic, clunky checkout journeys, ads running to the wrong page - you can spot the problems before they quietly drain sales.
 An encyclopedic knowledge of today’s martech, adtech, attribution, and analytics landscape. You don’t blindly trust one dashboard because it has a pretty graph. You understand tools like Triple Whale and GA4 can disagree, and you know how to contextualize performance instead of taking any single source as gospel.
 A strong grasp of testing strategy. A/B testing, multivariate testing, UX tests, offer tests, funnel tests, creative tests - you know how to plan tests that align with bigger roadmaps instead of throwing spaghetti at a wall and calling it “experimentation.”
 A solid understanding of UI/UX. This isn’t essential, but it’s a definite plus. You don’t need to be a designer, but you should understand how UX and UI choices affect customer behavior, conversion, trust, and campaign performance. And yes, we might swoon if you have it.
 A healthy respect for compliance, claims, and disclaimers. We work in the health space, which means “close enough” is not close enough. You’ll need to understand marketing claims, product basics, customer service considerations, and legal disclaimers well enough to keep campaigns accurate, compliant, and trustworthy.
 Now, time to be honest: is this really you? If you’re nodding your head and feeling that flutter of excitement, then we can’t wait to meet you.
 Other Qualities You’ll Need 
 At AlgaeCal, we’re going to insist that you have these 3 qualities:
 You’re humble–you put the team and others’ needs ahead of your own
 You’re hungry to learn more
 You’re people smart–in the sense that you’re a great teammate
 The truth is, if you don’t have these qualities, you won’t last long at AlgaeCal. So if you’re missing one of them, be honest. Save yourself a lot of headaches and skip to a job posting that is a better fit for you.
 What Will You Earn?  
 We believe in rewarding top talent. So let’s talk about salary once we’ve had the chance to get to know you better. Rest assured, we’re generous and offer above-market pay for the right person. If you bring the skills and experience, we’ll make sure the compensation reflects that.
 You’ll also enjoy the following benefits: 
 A generous healthcare package
 Monthly team events and activities
 Flexible Stat Holidays with the option to bank days for later use
 Weekly team lunches
 Casual dress code
 Incredible dog-friendly, Yaletown office one block from SkyTrain
 Remote working is okay with us too.
 And above all, you’ll join a team that you’ll never want to leave. Culture is everything to us. Yes, we work extremely hard to change as many people’s lives as possible. But we know how to have fun and reward ourselves too.
 How To Apply 
 So, do you have what it takes to become the next member of team AlgaeCal?
 Job opportunities like this don’t come along often, and we’ve got a lot to offer our successful applicant. So, to make sure our future Marketing Leader (Campaigns) Lead is the real deal, will be a great fit, and will thrive at AlgaeCal, we ask a little more than your run-of-the-mill job application:
 If this sounds like a position for you, please respond to this advertisement with your resume and cover letter. Please, read carefully:
 1. Write a cover letter addressing: 
 Why are you the best Marketing Leader (Campaigns) for this role? Give quantifiable examples of related achievements.
 Describe why you fit perfectly with our values. Read them here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1deCCJZ6tiDiOSlr_W0UdCuM_V_ahzPBs/view 
 What's the toughest challenge you’ve ever overcome in your life? How did you overcome it?
 What are the last three books you’ve read?
 What do you do for fun?
 2. Explain what you’re doing now for a job: 
  If you don’t have one, explain why.
  If you have one, explain why you’re looking elsewhere.
 3. Upload your cover letter and resume 
 Ensure that your cover letter and resume are saved and sent as one file.
 Yes, our hiring process is challenging, but it’s our way of selecting the best–and your way of ensuring your AlgaeCal teammates are tops.
 Click the “Apply Now” button on this page and upload your cover letter and resume. 
 ***Note: Please include your cover letter WITH your resume in one document. Applications without a cover letter will not be read!** *
 We are looking to hire as soon as we find the right person, so act quickly, and you can also expect a prompt response.

 Ce poste polyvalent couvre le cycle de vie complet de la sécurité : depuis l'évaluation d'architecture et l'intégration lors de projets majeurs (fusion-acquisition / M&A, onboarding applicatif, projets d'infrastructure) jusqu'au maintien en condition opérationnelle, à la gestion des vulnérabilités, la surveillance N3 et la coordination de crise cyber.

 Architecture Cible & Feuille de Route : Définir les architectures de sécurité cibles et les plans de migration conformes aux exigences et standards du Groupe.
 Onboarding Applicatif & Protections WAF : Piloter l'intégration des applications Web sur les plateformes de protection (Akamai WAF / App & API Protector, ASM, gestion des certificats et profils de trafic).

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!


WHY THIS TEAM?

Internal Infrastructure builds the infrastructure and tools used to train, evaluate, and serve Cohere's foundation models. You will work with AI researchers and ML engineers on stability, scalability, and observability. The work accelerates the models behind Cohere's platform, North.

You will build the platform that runs training, evaluation, and reinforcement-learning workloads: job lifecycle, scheduling, workload networking, and the storage those jobs depend on. The role includes a compensated 24x7 on-call rotation.


WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Own the platform that schedules and runs training, evaluation, and reinforcement-learning jobs on Kubernetes: who gets capacity, what happens when a job fails, and how a researcher finds out whether the platform caused it.

 - Build the networking and runtime isolation those workloads need, including agent and sandbox environments.

 - Work with the data infrastructure team on storage for checkpoints and other training artifacts.

 - Troubleshoot production failures and performance problems, and leave the system easier to operate than you found it.

 - Build automation, infrastructure-as-code, and observability so the platform stays maintainable.

We hire at more than one level. We set level based on the scope you've owned and how independently you drive work.


YOU MAY BE A GOOD FIT IF YOU HAVE

 - Run a job platform, batch system, or Kubernetes controllers in production. Scheduling, queues, and multi-tenant fairness are central to this work.

 ABOUT TRIVIUM
 Trivium Group is an Inc. 5000-ranked, Clutch Award-winning Amazon growth agency. We manage millions in ad spend and help brands scale profitably on the world's most competitive marketplace. Our closers don't take orders — they own the number. This is a small, high-performing team.
 THE ROLE
 This is a full sales cycle seat, not a closer-only seat.
 Qualified leads come to you. Demand is inbound heavy, generated through our own paid marketing across Amazon, Meta and Google, so warm leads land on your calendar — you don't have to find it. But if your calendar is light, you do not sit and wait. You work the list, you set your own calls, and you get the deal on the books. We are hiring someone hungry: someone who sees a lead and lets nothing get in the way of closing it and collecting the cash.
 You own the deal end to end: outreach and call-setting when needed, discovery, audit review, proposal, objection handling, close, and cash collection. Deals are monthly retainers in the $3,000–$7,000/month range, sold to e-commerce owners and operators.
 Who you'll be selling to: e-commerce entrepreneurs whose businesses range from a couple million a year to a couple million a month. You need to be able to hold a sales conversation with them as a peer — without pedestalizing them.
 YOUR NUMBER
 Cash collected is the #1 KPI. Not calls booked, not proposals sent, not pipeline created — cash collected. Close rate, average deal size, speed to close, and pipeline hygiene all support that one number.
 WHAT YOU'LL DO
 • Run the full cycle on inbound and referred demand — first call to signature to payment.
 • Set your own calls when the calendar has room. Follow up relentlessly on no-shows, stalls, and old leads.
 • Diagnose a prospect's e-commerce business live on the call and connect it to what we do.
 • Build and present proposals for monthly retainers, handle objections, and get signatures.
 • Own collection — a signed deal that doesn't pay is not a closed deal.
 • Keep the CRM clean and current: every deal, every next step, every dollar.
 • Work with the delivery team so what you sell is what gets delivered.
 WHO THIS IS NOT FOR
 • You only work leads that are already on your calendar.
 • You need a manager to tell you what to do each morning.
 • You cut corners on admin — CRM notes, Slack updates, end-of-day reports.
 • Your experience is one-call, one-time-payment consumer sales with no retainer track record.
 • You avoid the money conversation.
 OUTCOMES & KPIS
 Steady state, after ramp:
 • $30,000+ in new MRR cash collected per month, minimum.
 • 6–8 closed retainers per month, at a $4,000–$5,000/month average deal size.
 • 100% of signed deals paid — a signed deal that doesn't pay is not a closed deal.
 • 25%+ live call close rate (calls held to signed).
 • Speed to close: first call to signature within 14 days on qualified deals.
 • Average deal size held at or above $4,000/month.
 • Supported by 4–5 qualified calls a day, 5 days a week (about 100 held calls a month), with enough open calendar space to absorb full inbound demand and self-set calls when the calendar is light.
 TIME & LOCATION

 WHAT YOU NEED
 This is a senior, high-trust seat, and we are being deliberately selective.

 • Full sales cycle experience — you have set your own meetings, not just taken handed-off calls.

 • A self-starter. That includes proactively studying — advertising, e-commerce, and B2B sales, daily.

 • Comfortable being measured in public: cash collected, close rate, and pipeline hygiene are all visible.
 WHAT MAKES YOU STAND OUT
